content.text:
Read docs/STATE.md and docs/ROADMAP.md. Then run `entire checkpoint list` and
`entire checkpoint explain <most recent id> --full` for the reasoning behind the
latest work.

Do ROADMAP items 0 and 1, in that order. Item 0 first — item 1 depends on it.

ITEM 0 — the legal corpus must not be fetched at request time.
A previous attempt loaded the six core instruments per request and tripped Cala's
rate limit (HTTP 429). The corpus came back empty, and because the code requires a
citation, every claim collapsed to "unsupported". That was reverted.

Write scripts/corpus.ts that looks up the six instruments in CORE (exported from
lib/mooneto/laws.ts) ONCE, sequentially, with a delay between calls, and writes
data/corpus.json into the repo. Then change corpus() in laws.ts to read that file
and merge in any extra law the query names.

Verification that must pass before you commit: ask "Can I own a plot of land on the
Moon?" and confirm the settled count is NOT zero and that Moon Agreement claims now
cite the Moon Agreement. If everything comes back unsupported, the corpus failed to
load — do not ship it.

ITEM 1 — show the provision, not the blog.
Claims carry a `provision` object (law, year, text). app/page.tsx still renders the
old `sources` links pointing at blogs like newspaceeconomy.ca. Render the provision
as the evidence instead, and remove the blog links entirely — they are commentary,
not authority. Use the existing tokens in app/globals.css, no CSS framework.

Do not touch lib/mooneto/plan.ts or the memo rendering; those are done and verified.

Commit after each item with a message explaining the why. Every commit becomes an
Entire checkpoint.
I’ll first recover the project’s current state and the latest checkpoint rationale, then implement and verify item 0 before moving to the evidence UI in item 1.

+/** Legal provisions are the only authority Mooneto presents as evidence. */
+import bundledCorpus from "@/data/corpus.json"
+import { read, write } from "./cache"
+
+const API = "https://api.cala.ai"
+
+/** Generated into data/corpus.json by scripts/corpus.ts; never fetch this at request time. */
+export const CORE = [
+  "Outer Space Treaty",
+  "Moon Agreement",
+  "Artemis Accords",
+  "Rescue Agreement",
+  "Liability Convention",
+  "Registration Convention",
+]
+
+export type Provision = {
+  law: string
+  officialTitle?: string
+  year?: number
+  text: string
+}
+
+type LookupOptions = { useCache?: boolean; delayMs?: number }
+const pause = (ms: number) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms))
+
+async function call(path: string, init: RequestInit): Promise<any | null> {
+  const key = process.env.CALA_API_KEY
+  if (!key) throw new Error("CALA_API_KEY is not set")
+
+  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 3; attempt++) {
+    const res = await fetch(`${API}${path}`, {
+      ...init,
+      headers: { "X-API-KEY": key, "Content-Type": "application/json", ...init.headers },
+    })
+    if (res.ok) return res.json()
+    if (res.status !== 429 && res.status < 500) return null
+    await pause(1500 * (attempt + 1))
+  }
+  return null
+}
+
+/** Look up one Law entity. The generator can pace calls; runtime extras use the disk cache. */
+export async function lookupLaw(
+  name: string,
+  { useCache = true, delayMs = 0 }: LookupOptions = {}
+): Promise<Provision[] | null> {
+  const cacheKey = `law:${name}`
+  if (useCache) {
+    const cached = await read<Provision[]>(cacheKey)
+    if (cached) return cached
+  }
+
+  const found = await call(
+    `/v1/entities?name=${encodeURIComponent(name)}&entity_types=Law&limit=1`,
+    { method: "GET" }
+  )
+  const entity = found?.entities?.[0]
+  if (!entity) return null
+  if (delayMs) await pause(delayMs)
+
+  const detail = await call(`/v1/entities/${entity.id}`, {
+    method: "POST",
+    body: JSON.stringify({ properties: ["key_provisions", "official_title", "enactment_year"] }),
+  })
+  const props = detail?.properties ?? {}
+  const texts: string[] = props.key_provisions?.value ?? []
+  if (!texts.length) return null
+
+  const provisions = texts.map((text) => ({
+    law: entity.name,
+    officialTitle: props.official_title?.value,
+    year: props.enactment_year?.value,
+    text,
+  }))
+  if (useCache) await write(cacheKey, [], provisions)
+  return provisions
+}
+
+/**
+ * Merge the committed core corpus with any additional Law entities named by Cala.
+ * The only request-time lookups are non-core laws, and those are cached and sequential.
+ */
+export async function corpus(names: string[]): Promise<Provision[]> {
+  const core = bundledCorpus as Provision[]
+  const coreNames = new Set(core.map((provision) => provision.law.toLowerCase()))
+  const out = [...core]
+
+  for (const name of names.filter((law) => !coreNames.has(law.toLowerCase()))) {
+    try {
+      const provisions = await lookupLaw(name)
+      if (provisions) out.push(...provisions)
+    } catch (error) {
+      console.warn(`[laws] lookup failed for ${name}:`, error)
+    }
+  }
+  return out
+}
